prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create a single landscape 1536x1024 cinematic realistic historical painting in the AHOM project style. Subject: Joymoti's persecution at Jerenga Pathar, with her husband Prince Gadapani (later Gadadhar Singha) concealed at the jungle edge watching in anguish. This is an interpretive dramatic reconstruction, all subjects adults. Reference 1 defines Joymoti's face and muga-beige Assamese wrapped clothing with maroon borders; reference 2 defines ONLY Gadapani's face, moustache, goatee and long black hair, replace all royal clothing. Composition: near foreground at left, Gadapani crouches half concealed behind bamboo, ferns, cane and broadleaf lowland jungle foliage, face in three-quarter profile looking toward Joymoti. He wears a modest plain handwoven dark Naga-style wrap with narrow muted red stripes, simple waist wrap and cloth headband, no crown, no gold, no royal robe, no extravagant ceremonial headdress. In clearly readable middle ground, Joymoti stands fully clothed bound upright by rope around her waist and wrists to a solitary tree on a raised dry earthen patch in the middle of extensive flat paddy fields. Her posture and exhausted but resolute expression convey suffering. Two seventeenth-century Ahom guards in plain cream cotton and red waist sashes stand nearby, one sternly questioning her; a lowered cane is held at the guard's side. Depict the ordeal without an active blow, blood, open wounds, graphic injury, exposed body, or sexualized framing. Dignity and historical grief are central. Environment strictly Assamese Brahmaputra floodplain: flat rice paddies with muddy bunds and irrigation channels, distant bamboo groves, areca palms and low thatched rural houses, humid overcast afternoon light. Completely level horizon; NO hills, NO mountains, NO rocky cliffs, not even distant silhouettes. Rich natural textures, believable scale and eyelines linking the hidden husband to Joymoti, subtle depth, emotionally powerful respectful composition. No text, no watermark, no sheet layout.
notes: User-directed dramatic reconstruction. Tree restraint, concealed viewing position and Naga-style dress are interpretive; no specific community or authenticated period textile is claimed.
